en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Hammam Ismail Bin Hammam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘One secretive supplication of the servant equates to seventy supplications publicly’.
And in another report, (He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘A concealed supplication is more superior in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> than seventy apparent supplications’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from abu Hammam Isma’Il ibn Hammam from abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following: “

A servant’s praying and pleading before Allah for help, privately once, is equal to seventy such prayers in public.’ In another Hadith it is said: ‘A prayer that you (hide from people) is better before Allah than seventy prayers made in public.’”
